title: Sharp Volume Bounds in Picard Rank One and Polynomial Bounds for Log Calabi-Yau Surfaces
summary: For a complex $\varepsilon$-log canonical Fano surface of Picard number one, we prove that the anticanonical volume is at least $\varepsilon^2/100$ and that every integral nef and big Weil divisor has volume at least $\varepsilon^7/1728$. Both exponents are optimal. For $\varepsilon$-log canonical log Calabi--Yau surface pairs of arbitrary Picard number, we prove a lower bound of order $\varepsilon^9/(1+\log_2(1/\varepsilon))$, without a bigness assumption or further restrictions on the boundary coefficients.
